links.reason: The shared word is real: யார்க்கும் அணங்கு ஆதல் சான்றாள் (line 22) and the wives who guard their husbands and shut their doors (lines 24-26) against அணங்குகொல் in the couplet. But Kalittokai does not limit or condition the couplet's claim; it shares the word and the idea of beauty as an affliction, so the link is an image link and qualifies does not fit.

கண்டிகும் opens both (Ainkurunuru 121 line 1, Natrinai 20 line 1), a real formula shared. But Ainkurunuru 121 shows the woman leaping into the sea with her garland soaked (முண்டகக் கோதை நனைய, பௌவம் பாய்ந்து); nothing in the Tamil makes her 'a child at play', so the teaches sentence's contrast of spent lover and child is invented for one side.

இல்லோர் வாழ்க்கை இரவினும் இளிவு (line 2) ranks poverty as more shameful than begging, while Kural 1064 makes the refusal to beg when இடமில்லாக் காலும் the height of worth. On that plain reading the two rank the same states in opposite order, and the note names the reading. 'Explicitly reverses' is slightly strong, since the couplet praises the refusal rather than ranking the two states, but the claim holds.

Kar Narpathu 11 states the kodal as அணர்த்தெழு பாம்பின் தலைபோல், and Thinaimalai 107 has the kodal shrink in fear of the kaayaa taken for peacocks (மயிலென்று அஞ்சி), which works only through the same snake likeness, then carries it on to the ஐந்தலை நாகம் cloud. The image is conventional, but the comforting season sign becoming a chain of fear is shown in the Tamil.

Natrinai 88 does set aside யாம் செய் தொல் வினை (line 1) and proposes action (சென்று உரைத்தனம் வருகம்). But the thurai makes it speech for the hidden man, and the poem's weight is the hill weeping at his cruelty; 'the household's fatalism' is not in the poem. Fate overturned by effort is a shared topic stretched over a rhetorical move.

குன்றவர்கள் தந்தபெண் in the hymn and குறிஞ்சிக் குன்றவர் ... வள்ளி தமர் making a வித்தகத் தும்பை (Paripadal 9.67-68) are a real link through Valli's hill kin. But the hymn gives only a passing epithet; what the pair is said to show, the kin as partisans in the god's household, comes from the Paripadal alone.

Natrinai 289's நிலம் புடைபெயர்வதாயினும் கூறிய சொல் புடைபெயர்தலோ இலரே and Kural 1154's தெளித்தசொல் தேறியார்க்கு உண்டோ தவறு are two waiting women's responses to two absences; they make no incompatible claim about the same thing. Different stances in different situations are not a tension, and the teaches sentence comes down to the range of a waiting woman's speech, which is the shared topic.

Same king and a real shared catalogue of ruin: கடி காவின் நிலை தொலைச்சி and நெடுநகர் வீழ்ந்த in the idyll against கடிமரம் துளங்கிய காவும் and burnt நல்லில் in Purananuru 23. But the teaches claim that both measure conquest by 'animal couples' fails for Purananuru 23, whose doe has lost her stag to a tiger (அறுமருப்பு எழிற்கலை புலிப்பால் பட்டென); and Kalladanar's poem is itself a catalogue, not a 'single' image.

Same decade and the same giving of the girl: கொடுத்தனெம் ஆயினோம் (258) and கொண்டனர் செல்வர் (254). But Ainkurunuru decades are not narrative sequences, and reading 254 as the fulfilment of 258 imposes a story the Tamil does not give; 258 also ends on her unceased grief (இன்னும் ஆனாது நன்னுதல் துயரே).

Both turn on mistaking man for god: அருந்திறல் கடவுள் அல்லன் ... அணங்கியோனே (Ainkurunuru 182) and முருகு என உணர்ந்து (Akananuru 272). But 182 denies that a god caused her affliction, while 272's mother takes the visitor himself for Murugu, a reading the marker flagged as uncertain; the teaches sentence merges them into one 'habit' and adds the 'shore man's wreath' as something said in the poem.

A mated dove appears in both (மனைஉறை புறவின் செங்காற் சேவல் துணையொடு, Akananuru 254; புன்புறப் பேடை சேவல் இன்புற, Ainkurunuru 425), a common mullai homecoming image. In 425 the dove is road scenery the man drives through; nothing says he reads her longing in it, so 'each partner reads the other's longing' is not in the Tamil.

The idyll grants a பெருவறன் ஆகிய பண்பில் காலை, clouds that forget the sea (கடற்கோள் மறப்பவும்), and gives the harvest to காவிரி புரக்கும் நாடு; Kural 545 joins பெயலும் விளையுளும் to the just sceptre. On the reading that drought can fall even in this king's land, the two do conflict, and moving the harvest's source from rain to river is a real and specific observation.

Kural 1262 says if she forgets (இன்று மறப்பின்) her beauty leaves and her bangles slip; Kainnilai 58 says if she sits thinking of him (உள்ளி இருப்பின்) her bangles will not hold (பொறாஅ என் முன்கை வளை). The same sign is hung on opposite causes on the plain reading of each. 'Two traditions' is broad for two poems.

Kural 81 makes the household exist for விருந்தோம்பி, and Natrinai 41's friend, by the thurai's உலகியல், says men suffer far off because they want the life where the wife cooks for an எல்லி வந்த நல் இசை விருந்து. The pair shows the couplet's rule used as the reason for the separation, which neither verse shows alone.

Kural 1246 calls the heart's anger பொய்க்காய்வு because it yields at the sight of him; Ainkurunuru 151 grants the heart has melted (நெக்க நெஞ்சம்) and still refuses (நேர்கல்லேனே). The second does limit the first. Generalising this one poem to 'the Sangam woman's oodal' overreaches.

Both say memory will not fade: நெஞ்சு வடுப்படுத்துக் கெட அறியாது (Natrinai 357) and மறப்பறியேன் (Kural 1207). But வடு is itself a scar, a wound, and that she 'can bear the delay' comes from the thurai (ஆற்றுவல் என்பது படச் சொல்லியது), not the poem; so 'wound in one and support in the other' leans on the colophon.

Both are the man speaking to his charioteer on the homeward drive, Akananuru 34 urging செல்க தேரே and Kuruntokai 400 praising the driver who took புதுவழி across the gravel. They are poems by different poets, not 'the command and the thanks of one drive'; the charioteer's care (நன்றுபுரிந்து எண்ணிய மனத்தை) is Kuruntokai 400's alone, so the pairing adds the shared situation.

Both rebuke the season's thundering cloud with snakes struck by thunder (பாம்புபட இடிக்கும், Kuruntokai 158; பாம்பு பை மழுங்கல், Natrinai 238). Kuruntokai 158 argues from might (இமயமும் துளக்கும் பண்பினை), while Natrinai 238 argues from conduct (சான்றோர்ப் புரைவதோ அன்றே). That is a real and specific difference in how the reproach is made.

குறிப்பு is the only bond: Muthumozhikkanchi 100's lover does not give up குறிப்புச்சொல், while Kural 1097 reads the beloved's harsh words as the குறிப்பு of those who are close. They speak of different people's hints, so 'the speaker's practice and the hearer's skill' joins a shared word into a pairing the verses do not make.

The mother's நறிய நாறும் நின் கதுப்பு (Natrinai 143) and the foster mother picturing the lover weaving flowers into the hair (வெறிகமழ் பன்மலர் புனைய, Akananuru 117) do both read the bond in the girl's hair. But both mothers speak after the flight, and that the fragrance 'is' the lover's flowers of the other poem is an interpretive bridge.

The garland as evidence of another woman is real in both (கோதையின் உள் அழுத்தியாள் எவளோ, Paripadal 6.91-92; ஒருத்தியைக் காட்டிய சூடினீர், Kural 1313). The claim that the couplet was 'distilled from a festival' has no basis in either text, and the Paripadal speaker split is uncertain.

புறப்புண் நாணி is in both (65 line 10, 66 line 8): 65 mourns the king's death with a country that forgets its music and food, and 66 tells Karikal to his face, நின்னினும் நல்லன் அன்றே. The pair shows the loser ranked above the victor by the honour code, which neither poem gives so fully alone.

The same situation, private meeting turned public talk (கண் அறிவுடைமை அல்லது ... மூதூர் அறிந்தன்றோ இன்றே; கண்டது மன்னும் ஒருநாள் அலர்மன்னும்), which the brief marks as weak. The 'overhearing hero' pushing marriage comes from the thurai (சிறைப்புறமாக), not the poem.

Both turn on dusk and the absent partner: Kural 1222 asks if the evening's partner is வன்கண்ணது, and Kuruntokai 92's birds hurry home with food for their young (இரைகொண்டமையின் விரையுமால்). The contrast that only her man fails to come home is a fair implication, but it is the familiar dusk situation with a modest turn.

The same formula, கொற்கை ... முத்து and எயிறுகெழு துவர்வாய், is in both. Ainkurunuru 185 uses it as the man's praise, and Akananuru 27 says it may not hold him (தகைப்பத் தங்கலர் ஆயினும்) against the call of wealth. The limit is real. 'At first sight' is not stated in 185.

யாரையோ is in both: the shore lord's question in Natrinai 245 line 6 and the wife's estranged யாரையோ என்று இகந்து நின்றது in Natrinai 250 line 10. The reversal is neat, but it is one common interrogative, and that the words 'began the bond' is the friend's report of a first meeting; as a shared-word link it is thin for develops.

The plough figure is shared: நாஞ்சில் ஒப்ப நிலமிசைப் புரள (Purananuru 19 line 11) and வெள்ளிவெண் ணாஞ்சிலான் ஞால முழுவனபோல் (Kalavazhi 40). That Kalavazhi drops the mourners is true, but the history of a figure 'growing' once the kalavazhi became a genre is not shown by one pair.

Both refuse the night visit for fear of beasts (கடுமா தாக்கின், Ainkurunuru 296; குஞ்சரம் நடுங்கத் தாக்கி ... வாரல், Akananuru 92), which is the same situation. Akananuru 92 offers the millet day tryst outright (காவல் கண்ணினம் தினையே; நாளை), but Ainkurunuru 296's millet with the stealing peacock carries no such offer in its Tamil; reading it in is the generous reading.

Kural 1103 asks whether தாமரைக் கண்ணான் உலகு is sweeter than sleep on the beloved's arms, and Kuruntokai 288 asks whether புத்தேள் நாடு is sweeter even than இனத்தின் இயன்ற இன்னாமை. The second weighs heaven against love's pain, not its joy, so the claim is stronger; that is specific and true.

Akananuru 165's calf is not a buffalo calf beside its mother: lines 1-5 have an elephant calf whose mother fell into a pit (மடப்பிடி பயம்பில் பட்டென) drinking at a buffalo's udder (எருமை நல் ஆன் பெறுமுலை மாந்தும்). So the 'shared inventory' with Natrinai 271's buffalo calf asleep at home, and the 'calf safe beside its dam', misdescribe one verse. The playmates and the mother's wish to die (இறீஇயர் என் உயிர்; கழிக எற் கொள்ளாக் கூற்றே) are real shared signs.
links.text_issue: Akananuru 165 line 3 (எந்த) is unclear and the editions differ on its line count (13 against 12).

links.reason: நல்கின் வாழும் நல்கூர்ந்தோர் (Kuruntokai 327 line 1) answers Kural 1192's வாழ்வார்க்கு வானம் பயந்தற்றால் ... அளி: the one who lives by grace is denied it, and the water that does come is a தீய கலுழி tearing down the plantain. Grace as rain is shown from the side of its failure, which is specific.

Kural 744 makes a fort that which breaks the attacker's ஊக்கம், while the fragment lists wall, battlements, guard forest and moat and has the defenders lose heart (நெஞ்சுபுகல் அழிந்து). This is praise-poem hyperbole set against a definition of a good fort, not incompatible claims. It limits the couplet more than it contradicts it, though the observation about where morale is placed holds.

Pallor is used as an argument in both: பசத்தல் மற்று எவனோ against the friend's நல்லன் (Ainkurunuru 170) and பசப்பெனப் பேர்பெறுதல் நன்றே to shield him from blame (Kural 1190). These are different stances in different situations, which the brief says is not a tension. As a qualification the observation stands.

அறவர் for men who came முற்றா வேனில் முன்னி (Natrinai 86) and பொய்படு கிளவி நாணலும் எய்யார் when the செய்த பருவம் has come (Ainkurunuru 472) put a moral verdict on the return date either way. The pair shows the date judged as truthfulness, which is specific.

Neither verse is Sangam, and the link is a claim about Parimelazhagar's commentary, not about the two couplets: Kural 242's பல்லாற்றால் names no schools (the marker grants the ecumenical reading is his), and Kural 353 speaks of ஐயத்தின் நீங்கி with no conflict of systems. The teaches sentence describes a commentator's view, which the Tamil does not carry.

Akananuru 282's ivory, gold, gems and pearls describe the hill lord's country (... இழிதரும் நாடற்கு); the Tamil does not make them what wins எந்தையும் எதிர்ந்தனன் கொடையே. Thinaimozhi 50's coral and pearls heaped புகழக் கொணர்ந்து are not tied to the man at all. Reading them as awaited bride-wealth stretches both.

Both, by Kapilar, have the parrots mistake the girl's sound: கிளி அவள் விளியென எழல் ஒல்லா (Kuruntokai 291, from her clapper) and இன்குரல் கிளிசெத்து (Ainkurunuru 289, her voice). In 291 the man's delighted joke ends in her tears, and in 289 the friend follows it to the elders taking her off guard duty (காவலும் கடியுநர் போல்வர்) and so to வரைந்தனை கொண்மோ. The development is real.

Kural 414 offers கேட்க as the staff for one who has not studied (கற்றிலனாயினும்). Pazhamozhi 11 condemns the one who has neither studied nor heard from the learned, and gives his rare right judgement to luck (நாவற் கீழ்ப் பெற்ற கனி). The fallback becomes the minimum, which is specific and true.
links.text_issue: Line 1 prints சுற்றானும் சுற்றார்வாய்; the heading கல்லாதார் and the sense require கற்றானும் கற்றார்வாய்.

links.reason: Akananuru 16's wife asks the courtesan holding her son நீயும் தாயை இவற்கு?, and Kalittokai 84's other women, the boy's தாயர் (line 14), stop him in the street and give him a shark ring that the wife reads as a sign (குறி அறிந்தேன்). The son in the street as the channel between the women, courteous in one and hostile in the other, is specific.
links.text_issue: Kalittokai 84 lines 10-41 are not in the sangamtamil.com text.

links.reason: Eye-like flowers as a season sign are in both: கண்ணெனக் கருவிளை மலர (Ainkurunuru 464) and கண்மலர்போற் பூத்தன (Kar Narpathu 9). It is a common simile. The difference between messenger and calendar is real (இன்சொற் பலவும் உரைத்து against மறக்குநர் அல்லர்) but slight.
links.text_issue: Kar Narpathu 9 line 1 உருவினை is probably a corruption of கருவிளை.

links.reason: Kural 1215 makes waking and dream equally sweet கண்ட பொழுதே, and Kalittokai 68 likens the husband's embrace to கனவினான் எய்திய செல்வம், gone on waking (நனவினான் வேறு ஆகும்). Both hold that the pleasure lasts only while it is seen, so they are not incompatible; Kalittokai turns the point into an indictment, which qualifies the couplet rather than opposing it.

The drum-voiced rain is shared: வேந்தர் வென்றெறி முரசின் (Kuruntokai 380) and பணைமுழங்கு எழிலி (Akananuru 84). But Kuruntokai 380 says only that the lover is in a far land (நனிசேய் நாட்டர்); that the king's campaign is 'the cause' of his absence is read into a simile.

The same pair of similes, பொன் எனக் கொன்றை and மணி எனக் காயா, is in both. In Natrinai 242 it drives வல் விரைந்து செல்க பாக நின் தேரே, and in Ainkurunuru 420 the man promises to come and see the scrub with his woman (காணிய வருதும் யாமே வாள்நுதல் அரிவையொடு). The change from summons to leisure is in the Tamil, though 'once he is home' is inferred.

poems.note: Most of the poem is lost (lines 1, 2 and 4 are dotted gaps), so the rules cannot be applied.
The north wind is addressed directly and is the whole poem, so striking it leaves no stated sense.
Lines 3-4 are obscure, and no native thing acts in the poem.

The elephant herd, tired of the grove's plantain, raids the hamlet's jackfruit by day so that the hamlet cries out; this maps the man's day visits and the village talk they raise, the situation the thurai names (பகல் வருவானை இரவு வா).
The poem itself sets the adorned ford against the shoulders adorned with loneliness (அணிந்தன்று ... அணிந்தன்று), so the parallel is stated.

iraicchi.act: the waterfall carries sandal down to make the burnt clearing fragrant
iraicchi.sense: the deceitful lord's own falls tend a scorched field while he does not come to soothe her

poems.note: The flood is an event of the story (punal-tharu), not a vehicle.
The moon is addressed and the waning is joined to her shoulders by an open simile (என் தோள் போல்).

iraicchi.act: the dove calls again and again to its mate in delight
iraicchi.sense: in the season he named even the doves keep with their mates, which he fails to do

poems.note: The crow calling its kin may be heard as an omen of arrival, but that is a cultural sign, not an act of a person of the situation.

iraicchi.act: the tusker scoops the little water from the muddy rock pool and pours it over the head of the heat-wearied cow
iraicchi.sense: the man who takes that road will see such tending and be drawn back to care for her

iraicchi.act: the heron hunts food together with its mate and drops the fish into the mouths of its calling young
iraicchi.sense: with marriage at hand the lovers too will keep a household together

poems.note: The buffalo fleeing the drum could map the straying husband, but the poem states only his claim on her shoulders, not the straying.
